verdicts.reason: The arithmetic reproduces, but the mapping is not a bound. Per its own authors, the Planck+BOSS limit β < 0.0048 is set mainly by the background modification of the scalar model: the faster dilution of dark matter, which changes H(a) and the distance to last scattering. BOSS full shape adds little beyond Planck+BAO because the growth enhancement, an approximately constant amplitude shift, is degenerate with the linear bias b1. The gated model has no O(ε) background effect (K4). Matching its linear power excess to the ungated one at a single (k, z) therefore transfers none of what drives the published bound. The match point k = 0.2 h/Mpc is also the most favourable choice. At k = 0.1 h/Mpc the same gated ε gives an excess of only 0.9–2.6% (v* = 120–3000) against the ungated 3.7%. The 'BOSS-mapped' limits (0.0136 at 1000, 0.0068 at 3000 km/s) and the statement that the mapping beats Lyman-α above about 1000 km/s are unsupported.

missed_issues: The linear model is internally inconsistent. The density kernel R(y) = y∫sin(yt)W(t)dt belongs to the static effective potential W(r/s)/r. The anti-drag belongs to the stated −∇ₓU-at-fixed-velocities reading, whose own density kernel is R_A(y) = ∫₀¹R(yμ)dμ, which is 0.34–0.39 R near the pivot. gate_kernels.py checks R only against a sine transform of itself, never against the stated reading. Fixing this weakens every K6/K17 bound at v* ≤ 300 km/s by 1.5–2.3× (v* = 120: 0.0285 → 0.058, matter). This is distinct from the Lagrangian-reading question the agent flagged.

The cited fifth-force bounds (Archidiacono et al. 2022; Bottaro et al. 2024) are, by their authors' statements, driven by background geometry (the distance to last scattering, BAO), not by growth. BOSS full shape adds little beyond Planck+BAO because of the b1 degeneracy. So K9's power-excess mapping is not a bound, and K10's 'β < 0.0048 applies approximately' is unsupported.

The compressed test was not checked against the validity condition stated in its own source. DESI DR1 varies only A_s and n_s with the matter transfer function fixed, and claims no loss of information only within ΛCDM and some extensions. At the bound the gated model adds running of +0.054 to +0.061 at the pivot (ΛCDM: −0.187). Over 0.02–0.03 s/km it has 2–4% more power than the amplitude-plus-slope description; at 0.001–0.003 s/km it lacks the 2–6% deficit that description predicts. The direction of the resulting bias in the bound is not known without a P1D likelihood. Its redshift scaling, by contrast, is not a concern: T²(k_*) changes by less than 0.1% over z = 2.2–4.2.
K7 calls matter versus gas the largest systematic, but the reading/kernel choice at fixed tracer spans 0.021–0.058 at v* = 120, a factor of 2.7, as large as the matter–gas factor of 2.8–3.0.

K3 compares the 1D rms s1 with v*. The gate acts on the 3D |Δv|, whose rms at the gate radius is √3·s1: 69 km/s at z = 3 and 109–119 km/s at z = 1–0.5, comparable to v* = 120. The Hubble-flow gate is a good approximation at z ≳ 3 but not at z ≲ 1, which is where the BOSS mapping was placed.

The BOSS mapping matches at k = 0.2 h/Mpc, where the gated excess is largest. At k = 0.1 h/Mpc the same ε gives 0.9–2.6% (v* = 120–3000) against 3.7% ungated, so even as arithmetic the mapping is the most aggressive choice.

The Sgr translation uses the current speed, near pericentre. The orbit-time-averaged gate is 2.2× larger (0.144 against 0.066 at v* = 120), so ε < 0.70 rather than 1.52. Either way it is far weaker than Lyman-α; the KK 10% itself has no stated confidence level.

The thermal-velocity illustration omits the (4/11)^(1/3) e+e− entropy factor (6.1e-3 km/s at z = 1090, not 8.5e-3). The z_eq anchor compares two definitions; with ω_b+ω_c the computed z_eq is 3402.0, equal to Planck's.

The agent's kernel R overshoots 1 (R = 1.28 at k s_c = 2), so its model applies a density coupling above ε×gravity at k s_c ≈ 2. The stated-reading kernel R_A never exceeds 1. This is part of why the agent's bounds are tighter.

overall: Every number in the dark-tests analysis reproduces as the agent defined it, using independent code. The checks covered the background and gate radius, the EH98/BBKS spectra and pair velocities, a new two-fluid gated growth code, the DESI χ² bounds (≤1% agreement), the halo proxy, the satellite and Bullet gates by Monte Carlo, and Born scattering by direct integration. All literature values and quotes were found in the sources by live search. Three substantive problems remain. (1) The linear model mixes two readings of the potential. Its density kernel R = y∫sin(yt)W dt belongs to the static effective potential W(r/s)/r, while its anti-drag belongs to the stated reading (−∇ₓU at fixed velocities). The stated reading's density kernel is R_A = ∫₀¹R(yμ)dμ, which is 0.39 R at the pivot; brute-force checked. Applied consistently, it weakens the Lyman-α bounds at v* ≤ 300 km/s by 1.5–2.3×: 0.058/0.18 at 120 km/s instead of 0.0285/0.081. A fixed-peculiar-velocity reading instead gives 0.021/0.060. The reading spread (×2.7) is as large as the matter–gas bracket. (2) K9's BOSS mapping is not a bound. The authors of β < 0.0048 attribute it to the scalar background, which the gated model lacks, and say BOSS full shape adds little because of the b1 degeneracy. K10's 'β < 0.0048 applies' fails for the same reason. Above 1000 km/s the strongest computed limit is the DESI one, 0.017–0.035. (3) The compressed DESI test fixes the transfer-function shape, but at the bound the model adds running of +0.05–0.06 at the pivot (ΛCDM −0.187) and 2–4% extra power at 0.02–0.03 s/km, so all Lyman-α numbers remain estimates. The redshift-scaling assumption is fine (<0.1% change over z = 2.2–4.2). The conclusions that survive: percent-to-ten-percent limits on ε for 30 ≲ v* ≲ 3000 km/s; ε = 1 allowed only for v* ≲ 15–48 km/s depending on reading and tracer; satellites, the Bullet Cluster and scattering are never competitive. Minor corrections: 3D versus 1D pair velocities at z ≲ 1; the omitted e+e− entropy factor; the z_eq definition mismatch; the Sgr orbit-averaged gate (ε < 0.70); the extreme halo point (z_c ≈ 33–35).
